verdict.rationale: Omarchy's first-party manual guides installation: write the ISO to USB, answer five questions, with dedicated pages for dual-booting beside Windows and unattended installs, plus a VM image to try it first. The same manual teaches the desktop: the app launcher, the Omarchy Menu, terminal and browser hotkeys, Super + K for all key bindings, and tiling layout toggles. Community users report the install as uncomplicated and quick. Missing for 10: detailed step-by-step install walkthrough content in the evidence (the dual-boot and unattended pages are only linked, not shown), structured beginner tutorials for switchers, and independent corroboration that the docs themselves are helpful.

support.subject: As a switcher, I can follow guided tutorials to install the OS and learn the desktop interface

citations.quote: Write the ISO to a USB stick and answer five questions. It hands back a finished desktop.
The manual also covers [dual booting beside Windows](/manual/dual-boot-install/) and [unattended installs](/manual/unattended-installs/).
you can hit `Super + Space` to reveal the application launcher and `Super + Alt + Space` to open the Omarchy Menu.
You can see all the main keyboard bindings with `Super + K`.
the install is uncomplicated with no bootloader or WM choices
